title: Analyzing Occupational Gender Bias across the LLM Training Lifecycle
abstract: arXiv:2610.23587v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Post-training is widely assumed to reduce the social biases language models inherit from pretraining, yet direct evidence for this assumption remains mixed. In this paper, we examine how gender disparities evolve across the language modeling pipeline. In particular, we study occupational gender bias in OLMo 3, a fully open language model family, across its post-training stages by prompting each checkpoint to generate open-ended narratives about synthetic personas given their occupation and education. We consider two settings, a gender-given setting in which the profile states the persona's gender explicitly and a gender-assumed setting in which it must be inferred by the model. We find that when gender is stated, post-training increases semantic diversity for male-coded profiles, whereas for female-coded profiles the increase is smaller after SFT and not significant after DPO and RLVR. translated_title: 分析大语言模型训练全生命周期中的职业性别偏见
translated_abstract: 后训练被普遍认为能够减少语言模型从预训练中继承的社会偏见，然而支持这一假设的直接证据仍然不一致。在本文中，我们研究了性别差异如何在语言建模流程中演变。具体而言，我们让完全开源的语言模型家族OLMo 3在各个后训练检查点上，根据合成人物的职业和受教育背景生成开放式叙述，从而研究其职业性别偏见。我们考虑了两种设定：一种是“给定性别”设定，即人物档案中明确标注人物性别；另一种是“推断性别”设定，即性别需要由模型自行推断。我们发现，当性别被明确给出时，后训练提升了男性编码人物档案的语义多样性，而对于女性编码人物档案，SFT之后的提升幅度较小，且在DPO和RLVR之后不再显著。当性别由模型推断时，后训练……
tldr: 通过分析完全开源的OLMo 3模型在后训练各阶段生成的合成人物叙述，本研究发现后训练对职业性别偏见的影响并不对称——它显著提升了男性编码人物叙述的语义多样性，但对女性编码人物的提升在SFT后较小、在DPO和RLVR后不显著，表明后训练缓解性别偏见的效果有限。
en_tdlr: By analyzing open-ended persona narratives generated across the post-training stages of the fully open OLMo 3 model family, this study finds that post-training affects occupational gender bias asymmetrically—increasing semantic diversity for male-coded personas while yielding smaller or insignificant gains for female-coded ones—suggesting that post-training's ability to mitigate gender bias is limited.
